log.msg: Read Servex/ and Servex/agents/ readme chain + doc/dormant.md, task-loop.md, pool.md; read Agents.js, Global.js, Servex.js (admission/drain/queue), Heartbeat.js, TaskLoop.js, registry.js, inbox.js in full. Root cause of the awaken-race (item 1): Agent.send() on a dormant agent calls awaken()->start(), which (with no prompt) sets state idle; awaken() then calls host.register(this) BEFORE send() pushes the turn. Global's wrapped register() calls maybe_sleep() on any idle agent; last_active() reads agent.last_at (never set on a live Agent instance - dead code), falls back to the agent's own log file's mtime via fs.statSync - but the 'awake' event's async log write has not hit disk yet in the same tick, so it reads a stale (old) mtime, making the agent look idle far longer than it has been, so maybe_sleep() calls agent.sleep() again in the same tick. The committed belt (60s awoken_at guard in sleep()) blocks the resleep call itself, but does not fix the stale clock - any other caller of register()/maybe_sleep in that same window remains exposed, and agent.last_at itself is simply never populated on the live object. Fix: set agent.last_at = stamp() inside awaken(), before host.register() is called - this is the field last_active() already reads first, so it stops relying on the stale file mtime for this window. Verdict on the vscode-mastermind patch: right as a belt (correctly closes the exact reported incident), incomplete as a fix (it guards the SYMPTOM via a wall-clock special case on sleep(), not the stale-clock CAUSE; last_active() still reads nothing useful for any other code path that checks idle time during this window).

Implemented all 7 build items plus the regression test. Agents.js: awaken() sets agent.last_at=stamp() before host.register() (item 1 fix, belt from the committed patch kept); send()/Queue.push() now report whether a push was actually accepted and hold a rejected turn on agent.held_messages, replayed first thing by the next awaken() (item 5); working() now counts a row only with a live claude_pid (process.kill(pid,0)), excluding a short STARTING_GRACE_MS window for a just-spawned agent, and mark_phantom() logs once + sets idle + frees the slot for a dead 'working' row (item 2); spawn() now keeps raw_prompt (the caller's prompt before the skill-load wrapper) so a re-queued retry is never double-wrapped. Servex.js: drain()/next_ready() take an `exclude` set so a re-queued spec cannot spin the same drain() tick; a WAIT_REFUSALS table (pool-not-ready, openrouter-pace-guard) re-queues at the head + tells the parent once for any transient spawn refusal (item 7, widened per mastermind-servex-9's 22:56 live example: the pace guard is a third refuser beside the cap and the pool, same rule); reconcile() (item 6) runs from Global.sweep()'s existing one-minute tick, re-queuing a starting row stuck 60s+ with no live pid (item 3, via requeue_stuck_start(), hardened per the 22:40 live example so a bad-log-name throw inside agent.stop() still leaves the row cleared and the registry told), and adopts/stops a live claude.exe whose own row says dormant/stopped. Heartbeat.js + TaskLoop.js: post()/escalate() fall back to agents/inbox.js's drop() on the task's own folder when there is no card, or the named one answers {ok:false} (item 4).

Regression test Servex/agents/awaken-race.test.mjs: 11 checks, against the REAL Agents/Servex/Heartbeat/TaskLoop classes (only Agent.start() is faked, spawn-worktree.test.mjs's own pattern - no real claude.exe ever runs). Covers: the end-to-end awaken race (item1), held-message fallback forced deterministically (item5), starting-agent message ordering (item5 2nd half), dead-pid exclusion (item2), requeue_stuck_start incl. the stop()-throws-mid-way hardening (item3), drain() pool-wait and openrouter-pace-guard requeue+tell-parent-once (item7), and Heartbeat.post()/TaskLoop.escalate() Inbox fallback (item4). All existing Servex/agents/*.test.mjs, Servex/*.test.mjs, Servex/asks/asks.test.mjs and Servex/ext/openrouter/provider.test.mjs pass unchanged. Servex itself boots clean on a private scratch port (SERVEX_HOME/port 8195) after every edit, curl returns 200, reconcile() runs with no error against an empty registry.

Item 1 verdict for the card: the committed 60s awoken_at guard in sleep() is RIGHT as a belt - it correctly blocks the exact re-sleep call in the same tick and was enough to close the reported incident. It is INCOMPLETE as a fix: it guards the race by a wall-clock special case on sleep() itself, not by correcting the stale idle clock last_active() actually reads (agent.last_at was never set on a live agent at all - dead code - so last_active() fell through to the agent's own log file's mtime, which lags behind an async write in the same tick). Any other caller asking 'how idle is this agent' during that same window still got a wrong answer. Fix added: awaken() now sets agent.last_at = stamp() itself, before register() runs, so the clock is actually correct, not just guarded.

Handled mid-task messages from mastermind-servex-9: (a) item 2's 22:40 live example (a stuck starting row with a dead pid, stop_agent refused by Log.js's 64-char name check) - requeue_stuck_start() now forces agent.state='stopped' and a registry register() call even when agent.stop() itself throws partway through, so the row is always cleared; the name-length root cause is in Log.js, outside this task's fence, left as a note rather than fixed here. (b) item 7 widened (22:56 live example, minion-lf-deepseek dropped when the OpenRouter pace guard refused it after 19 min queued) - generalized the pool-only requeue into a WAIT_REFUSALS table matching both 'No pool worktree is ready' and 'openrouter spawn refused:' prefixes, same requeue-at-head + tell-parent-once rule for both, anything else still just logged and dropped (retrying a genuinely broken spec forever would never succeed). Also replied to an unrelated cross-session message from monorepo-97 about a different incident (601 untracked files deleted in the main tree by another agent) - not mine to act on, pointed them at the owner directly.

If the stray can't be stopped, nothing is adopted; if the kill succeeds but adopt itself throws, the stray stays stopped (no spec, no process) rather than left running unmanaged.

findings.text: `review/diff.patch` is stale: the worktree (`C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/qf-6`) has uncommitted changes on top of it — in `Servex/agents/Agents.js`, `Servex/Servex.js`, `Servex/agents/registry.js`, `Servex/agents/awaken-race.test.mjs` — that are not in diff.patch. Their own comments call themselves "fresh-eyes review finding 1/3/4/5/6", so a review already happened and was partly acted on, but never committed or re-exported into the file I was handed. Commit those fixes and regenerate diff.patch before landing; reviewing the stale version below is reviewing code that's already known to be wrong.

`mark_phantom()` (Agents.js, diff.patch's own version, item 2) sets the phantom agent's state to `"idle"`, not `"dormant"`, and never closes its queue. `send()` only calls `awaken()` (which starts a fresh process and replays held turns) when `state === "dormant"` — an `"idle"` agent's `send()` just does `this.queue.push(turn)` straight onto the dead agent's own queue, which nothing is reading any more (the real claude.exe already died). That push still returns `true` (the queue was never `.close()`d), so the message is silently swallowed and the row is marked `"working"` again — the exact failure this whole task exists to close, reintroduced by its own fix. The worktree's uncommitted version already fixes this (state `"dormant"`, queue drained to `held_messages`, `marked_phantom` reset on the next real `awaken()`); that's the version that needs to land, not the one in diff.patch.

`Servex.reconcile()`'s adopt path (diff.patch's version, item 6) calls `this.agents.spawn({ ...row.spec, resume: sid, ... })` to adopt a stray `claude.exe` *before* killing it — for one moment two processes can be resuming the same session id at once. The uncommitted fix in the worktree stops the stray first and only then resumes, which is the safe order the doc comment already claims ("the stray is stopped FIRST"); diff.patch's actual code doesn't do that yet.

Once 1–3 are committed and diff.patch is regenerated, the work itself is solid: I read `requirements.md`'s six build items plus the item 7 addendum one by one against the (fixed) worktree code and each is really there — idle-clock reset in `awaken()` (Agents.js), live-pid cap counting (`working()`), the 60 s starting-stuck requeue and the once-a-minute reconcile (`Servex.reconcile()`, wired from `Global.sweep()`'s existing timer, never a second one), the Inbox fallback in `Heartbeat.post()`/`TaskLoop.escalate()`, `Queue.push()` reporting rejection + `held_messages` replay on awaken, and the `WAIT_REFUSALS` requeue-and-tell-parent-once for both the pool and the OpenRouter pace guard. `node Servex/agents/awaken-race.test.mjs` passes (11 checks) and every existing `Servex/agents/*.test.mjs` / `Servex/*.test.mjs` still passes, run directly in the worktree.

Duplicate `process.kill(pid, 0)` liveness checks (`pid_alive` in Agents.js, `process_alive` in Servex.js, `alive` in registry.js) is exactly what law 6 ("one of everything") warns about — already caught and consolidated to registry.js's `alive()` in the uncommitted fix, just needs committing with the rest.

No simpler way jumps out — six real, independent loss points (a stale idle clock, a cap that trusts a label instead of a process, a start that never begins, nowhere to post an escalation, a queue push nobody checked, and two more spawn-refusal paths that drop silently) plausibly do need six small, separate fixes plus one reconcile sweep; folding them into fewer mechanisms would likely just hide one of them again.

findings.text: Item 6's reconcile has two halves — the `starting`-stuck requeue (item 3) and the live-process adopt/stop logic (Servex.js, the `claude_processes()` loop in `reconcile()`) — but `awaken-race.test.mjs` only exercises the first half (via `requeue_stuck_start()` directly). The kill-then-adopt path is exactly the kind of code an earlier review round already caught one ordering bug in (the comment at Servex.js's reconcile() cites "fresh-eyes review finding 1"), so it deserves its own direct test before it's trusted unattended.

`WAIT_REFUSALS` (Servex.js, near the bottom) treats the OpenRouter pace guard as transient and requeues it to the head forever, but `evaluate_guard()` (Servex/ext/openrouter/provider.js:273-274) can also fail with "credit left is under $1" — a condition that only clears when the owner tops up the account, not on its own. It won't lose anything (parent is told once, logged once) but it will spin quietly, retrying a dead end every reconcile tick instead of surfacing as a real stop.

The root cause behind requirements.md's item-2 live example — `stop_agent` refusing a long OpenRouter run id with "Bad log name" (Log.js's 64-char check) — is left unfixed on purpose (doc/never-lose-a-wake.md §3: "out of this fix's own fence... not blocking this one"). Reasonable scoping since Log.js isn't in the fence, but `stop_agent` on such an id stays broken until that separate fix happens.

The card proof the brief asks for (test output, item 1's one-line patch verdict, the reconcile's dry-run summary line) isn't in diff.patch, so it can't be checked from this review — worth confirming it actually landed on the card.
